requirements.requirement: The offline evaluation harness must execute scenario suites against an AI system and grade the results.
requirements.brief_evidence: “We need a diagram of how our offline evaluation harness executes scenario suites against an AI system and grades the results.”

representation_evidence.observation: The main flow proceeds from pinned suite inputs through isolated scenario execution, outcome classification, grading, scorecard assembly, and comparison.

representation_evidence.locator: objects and connections; sections pinned-inputs, bounded-execution, evidence-grading, assembly-comparison
representation_evidence.observation: The JSON contains a connected orchestration from pinned-suite and scheduler through isolated-sut, grade-dispatch, graders, assembler, scorecard, and comparison.

requirements.requirement: Each run must start from a pinned suite containing frozen scenario definitions.
requirements.brief_evidence: “Each run starts from a pinned suite containing frozen scenario definitions…”

representation_evidence.observation: The section contains “Pinned suite” and an “Immutable scenarios” note, and the run-start flow begins from these pinned inputs.
The pinned-suite object is paired with a rule stating that scenarios are immutable, and its flow leads through the run fingerprint to the scheduler.

requirements.requirement: The pinned run must include a fingerprint of the tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions.
requirements.brief_evidence: “…and a fingerprint of the tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions.”

representation_evidence.locator: Section “1 · Pinned run inputs,” object “Run fingerprint”
representation_evidence.observation: A run fingerprint is clearly present and participates in starting the run, but its four required constituent fields are not shown.

representation_evidence.locator: object[fingerprint], canvas description, and all object text/annotations searched for revision, configuration, prompt, and rubric version fields
representation_evidence.observation: The JSON includes a generic “Run fingerprint” object and describes a fingerprinted suite, but no object, note, annotation, or field enumerates tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions.

requirements.note: The fingerprint itself is represented, but its stated composition is omitted.

requirements.requirement: Scenario wording changes must create new scenario versions rather than editing scenarios in place because wording changes invalidate historical comparisons.
requirements.brief_evidence: “Because wording changes invalidate historical comparisons, scenarios receive new versions instead of being edited in place.”

representation_evidence.locator: Section “1 · Pinned run inputs,” blue note below the input objects
representation_evidence.observation: The note states “Immutable scenarios” and “Wording changes create a new scenario version.”
The text explicitly says scenarios are immutable and wording changes create a new scenario version.

The scheduler-to-worker-pool connection is directed forward and labeled “bounded fan-out.”

The isolated target is explicit, and the note explicitly excludes the shared production instance.

representation_evidence.observation: The path is labeled “ordered steps,” and the note says workers execute ordered scenario steps.
Both the connection label and note explicitly encode ordered scenario-step execution.

representation_evidence.observation: “Promote compatible run” connects to “Chosen baseline” with “becomes,” which then connects to “Future compatible runs” with “used by.”

representation_evidence.locator: objects[promote-run, chosen-baseline, future-runs] and connections[c-promote-baseline, c-baseline-future]
representation_evidence.observation: The directed lifecycle exactly shows promotion becoming the chosen baseline and being used by future compatible runs.

verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: Bounded isolated execution and failure-semantics separation are especially complete: scheduler fan-out, bounded workers, isolated non-production SUT, ordered capture, infrastructure retry, product-failure record-and-continue, and preserved outcome distinction are all explicit.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: R3 is only partial: the board includes a run fingerprint but does not identify its required contents—tested revision, configuration, prompt versions, and rubric versions. The other gap is R20's missing narration output for threshold-crossing movements.
verdict.coverage_summary: The board represents nearly the entire operational contract, including immutable pinned scenarios, bounded isolated execution, evidence-backed concurrent grading, compatible baseline comparison, audit retention, and baseline promotion. Two requirements are partial: the fingerprint is not decomposed into its stated versioned inputs, and threshold movement is shown without the required narration. Weighted coverage is 43.5/45 = 0.9667; no absent or contradicted system-defining requirement triggers a cap.
